record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.original_question:
Let p be an e-hyperbolic polynomial with p(e)=1, where e ∈ R^n, and
let v1 and v2 lie in the positivity cone C_p(e)^+ of
p with respect to e. Must all Taylor coefficients of the two-variable
function (z1, z2) ↦ -log(p(e - z1 v1 - z2 v2)) be
nonnegative?

evidence.quote: Problem 41 ([14, 15]). Let p be an e-hyperbolic polynomial for which p(e) = 1, where e ∈ Rn , and suppose that v1 , v2 are in the positivity cone Cp (e)+ of p w.r.t. e.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a homogeneous polynomial that is hyperbolic with respect to a vector $e \in \mathbb{R}^n$; that is, $p(e) \neq 0$ and for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ the univariate polynomial $t \mapsto p(te - x)$ has only real roots. Normalize so that $p(e) = 1$. The (open) hyperbolicity cone of $p$ with respect to $e$ is
$$C_p(e)^+ = \{ v \in \mathbb{R}^n : \text{all roots of } t \mapsto p(te - v) \text{ are positive}\}.$$
Let $v_1, v_2 \in C_p(e)^+$. Consider the two-variable real-analytic function
$$F(z_1, z_2) = -\log\, p(e - z_1 v_1 - z_2 v_2),$$
defined for $(z_1, z_2)$ in a neighborhood of the origin in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Prove or disprove: every Taylor coefficient of $F$ at the origin is nonnegative, i.e., for all integers $k_1, k_2 \geq 0$,
$$\frac{\partial^{k_1+k_2} F}{\partial z_1^{k_1} \, \partial z_2^{k_2}}\bigg|_{(0,0)} \geq 0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The two-vector hyperbolic analogue is known to be equivalent (via the Lax conjecture/theorem for hyperbolic polynomials in two variables) to the classical Bessis–Moussa–Villani (BMV) conjecture, which was proved by Herbert Stahl in 2011 (with simplified proofs by Eremenko and others). The corresponding statement for three or more vectors is known to be false. Hence the two-vector version stated here is settled affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Stahl's theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Stahl's theorem is a theorem proved in 2011 by Herbert Stahl concerning the BMV conjecture, originally posed in 1975.
status_evidence.claim: BMV conjecture has been proved by Stahl.

status_evidence.title: Herbert Stahl's proof of the BMV conjecture (Eremenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Simplified proof of Stahl's theorem establishing the BMV conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Independent simplified proof confirming BMV is proved.

status_evidence.title: AIM workshop report: Polya-Schur-Lax problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problems 40–41 (two-variable / two-vector hyperbolic analogue) are equivalent to the BMV conjecture; the three-or-more analogue is false.
status_evidence.claim: The two-vector hyperbolic analogue is equivalent to BMV.
